clue.text: Confined in twin cots

parts.note: a crib is a child's cot, the first of the pair
a cot is also a small bed, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A pair of babies kept penned in their matching cots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twin' is the trick: it asks for two different words that each mean cot, joined end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbed means shut up in a narrow space, as in Macbeth's 'cabined, cribbed, confined'.

clue.text: Charles X's discipline

parts.note: Chas is the short form of Charles
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: The strict rule of a French king, Charles the Tenth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charles X' looks like a king's name; it splits into CHAS and the Roman numeral, while 's means is, so the second half is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to correct or punish so as to improve, which is what to discipline means.

clue.text: Hold on, appearing to sway

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a power or grip over someone
second meaning: to affect someone's decisions

explanation.surface: Someone told to wait while they wobble.
explanation.walkthrough: The first phrase looks like a request to wait; here it is a noun phrase, as in having a grip on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Influence as a noun is power over another, and as a verb it means to affect or bend opinion.

clue.text: Sounds like the night Toby let this out

definitions.text: Sounds like the night Toby let this out

parts.note: surface reading: an echo of some noise, as if a homophone follows
setter's reading: the knight Sir Toby of Twelfth Night, whose surname is also a noisy burp

explanation.walkthrough: 'the night' points to Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, and its Toby is the knight Sir Toby, whose surname is the sound in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A belch is the noisy release of wind from the stomach, a sound a drunken reveller lets out.

clue.text: This title-holder is unlikely to be in practice

definitions.text: This title-holder is unlikely to be in practice

parts.note: surface reading: a sports champion who has stopped training
setter's reading: an academic doctor, not a medical one who runs a practice

explanation.walkthrough: The title is Dr, and the one who holds it here earned it by research, so has no surgery to run.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctorate is the highest university degree, which entitles a scholar to be called doctor without treating patients.

clue.text: There's only one name for awful meanness in a host

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so its letters are jumbled
the word that follows has two of the letter for name, and only one may stay

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comment that a crowd of mean people share just one name between them.
explanation.walkthrough: MEANNESS has two Ns; leaving only one gives MEANESS, which is rearranged into EN MASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase en masse means all together as a group, as a crowd or host would move.

clue.text: Gave a sedative internally and relieved pain

definitions.note: a verb with its object; the answer means relieved, of pain

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so the letters lie inside the words before

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and into the last

explanation.surface: A nurse injects a calming drug and the patient's pain goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to make pain or distress lighter, so eased is relieved suffering.

clue.text: What time is the average interval?

definitions.note: the answer names the time in between, as a question reply

parts.note: the mean is the arithmetic average
a while is a period or space of time

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking how long a typical break lasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a pun: the time in between is literally a mean while.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanwhile as a noun is the intervening time, the period during which something else happens.

clue.text: Drink, the support of the weaker members

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cocktail of spirit, water and sugar

definitions.text: the support of the weaker members
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a cloth band that holds up an injured arm

explanation.surface: A bar where the stronger regulars prop up the feeble ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' sounds like people in a club; here they are limbs, and an injured arm rests in a sling.
explanation.definitionFit: A sling is both a sweetened spirit drink and a bandage looped round the neck to cradle a hurt arm.

clue.text: He puts up the scaffold for eastern holy man

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A builder of gallows hired on behalf of a holy man from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is one who builds or raises structures, such as the frame of poles round a building.

clue.text: Authorised to be executed — how ghastly

definitions.note: an exclamation; the answer is the adjective inside it

indicators.note: an executed person is beheaded, so the word loses its head letter

parts.note: something authorised is permitted by law

explanation.surface: Someone's death sentence has been legally approved, and the observer is horrified.
explanation.walkthrough: Execution here means beheading: LAWFUL loses its first letter to leave AWFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and ghastly are synonyms for something very bad or shocking; 'how awful' is the same cry.

clue.text: Pitch a team have to give up using

parts.note: to pitch is to throw
taken as written
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A sports team told they must stop using their home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like the sports field, but here it is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast something aside is to discard or abandon it, so you stop using it.

clue.text: Superstitious advice to a firelighter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the phrase said, with a tap on something wooden, to keep luck from turning
second meaning: dry rotten wood or fungus used as tinder

explanation.surface: A warning to someone lighting a fire not to tempt fate.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word, touchwood is old tinder; as two words it is the lucky saying, so the 'advice to' a firelighter is really a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch wood is the British form of knock on wood, and touchwood is also punk or tinder that catches a spark.

clue.text: Island creature

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Isle of ..., off England's south coast
second meaning: an archaic word for a living being

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island in the English Channel; wight is an old word for a person or creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The proper name of an English island and an archaic noun for a being share one spelling.

clue.text: Refusals about new office

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: noes are votes or answers of no
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone turns down several offers for a new office job.
explanation.walkthrough: Office here is the church sense: a set service of prayers said at a fixed hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nones is the canonical hour said at mid-afternoon, one of the daily offices of prayer in monasteries.

clue.text: Colt?

parts.note: surface reading: a young male horse, the offspring of a stallion
setter's reading: a Colt is a make of revolver, so a young colt would be a firearm's offspring

explanation.walkthrough: A colt is a male foal, and Colt is also a famous revolver brand, so a small colt is the child of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The old exclamation and mild term for a rascal, read literally as the offspring of a firearm.

clue.text: Electronic device — not a standard lamp, if that's right

indicators.note: not standard means not in the usual form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone describing an electrical gadget that isn't quite an ordinary standard lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: A standard lamp is a British floor lamp; here 'standard' just signals that LAMP IF is reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: An amplifier is an electronic unit that boosts a signal, a typical piece of electronic equipment.

clue.text: Rather small, say, for a biscuit

parts.note: petit is French for small

indicators.note: say means as it is spoken, so the word goes by its pronunciation

parts.note: the preposition is pronounced like the number

explanation.surface: Someone apologising that a cookie is rather on the small side.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'for' joins the clue to the biscuit; it is really wordplay, spoken like the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A petit four is a small fancy cake or biscuit served with coffee after a meal.

clue.text: With two sides equal, is very large island to be abandoned?

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so the word be is dropped from the name

parts.note: taken as written
OS is short for outsize, a clothing size
Celebes is the former name of Sulawesi in Indonesia

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle over whether a big island ought to be deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be abandoned' works literally: the letters BE are taken out of CELEBES.
explanation.definitionFit: An isosceles triangle is one having two of its sides of the same length.

clue.text: Country where one does not expect developments

definitions.text: Country where one does not expect developments

parts.note: surface reading: a nation where nothing new ever happens
setter's reading: countryside around a town where housing developments are forbidden

explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is not a nation but countryside, and 'developments' are building projects, not news.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a protected ring of open land round a city where building is restricted by planning law.

clue.text: Boastful talk to excite a producer of hot air

parts.note: gas is empty, bragging chatter
to fire someone up is to rouse them

explanation.surface: A windbag whose bragging is meant to stir up a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot air' looks like more boastful talk; here it is literal heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas fire is a domestic heater burning gas, which literally warms the room's atmosphere.

clue.text: Echo somehow captures opening of Pleistocene age

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it inside
somehow suggests done in some unknown way, so the letters come in another order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the geological period's name

explanation.surface: A geologist hearing echoes from the dawn of the Ice Age.
explanation.walkthrough: ECHO is rearranged to EOCH, which then takes P inside after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period of history or geological time, so it means an age.

clue.text: Little change to be expected at football matches?

definitions.text: Little change to be expected at football matches?

parts.note: surface reading: hardly anything different happening during a game
setter's reading: small coins worth half a penny, and a football match comes in halves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Little change' is small coinage, and the match link is that a game of football is split into two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Ha'pence are halfpennies, the old British coins worth half a penny, about the smallest change there was.

clue.text: Scratch back of neck right away

indicators.note: away means gone, so the letter named is taken out

parts.note: the scruff is the nape, the back of the neck
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone scratching an itch at the back of their neck at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as immediately, but it means remove R: SCRUFF without R is SCUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuff is a mark rubbed or scraped on a surface, much like a light scratch.

clue.text: Bare head and take top off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to remove one's hat
second meaning: to remove the lid of a bottle or pen

explanation.surface: Someone baring their head and opening a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncap is to remove a cap, whether a hat from the head or a lid from a container.

clue.text: The dairymaid's prize flower?

parts.note: setter's reading: a trophy cup won for the best churned produce at a show
surface reading: the bloom a milkmaid treasures most

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer and it is a cup awarded for dairy produce; whole, it is a yellow meadow flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wild flower of pastures, and the name also parses as a dairy trophy.

clue.text: Toves' companion, I note, lost a fish

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so these letters drop out

parts.note: Carroll's Jabberwocky opens: 'Twas brillig, and the slithy toves
taken as written
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A line about a Jabberwocky creature losing a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: BRILLIG loses I and G from its end to leave BRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is a European flatfish related to the turbot, eaten as a food fish.

clue.text: To an audience, Anouilh may signify mental weariness

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word goes by its sound

parts.note: the French playwright's surname is pronounced on-wee

explanation.surface: A theatre audience finds a play by Jean Anouilh tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Anouilh was a French dramatist; his name, said aloud, matches the French word for boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom and dissatisfaction, a weariness of the mind rather than the body.

clue.text: Got coin in exchange from Bunbury, for example

definitions.note: loose: an incognito is a person using a false identity, as the name stands for

indicators.note: an exchange swaps things about, so these letters change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone paid in coins in a deal struck in the market town of Bunbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunbury looks like a place; it is the imaginary invalid friend in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, a cover for travelling under false pretences.
explanation.definitionFit: Going incognito means concealing your true identity, which is what visiting Bunbury lets Algernon do.

clue.text: Man-made fibre in name only perhaps

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name

indicators.note: perhaps means maybe in some other form, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sneer that a synthetic fibre is a fabric only in name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in name only' reads as a stock phrase; break it to get N followed by a rearranged ONLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer spun into thread, the first fully man-made textile fibre.

clue.text: Put on jury to measure penal reform

parts.note: an em is a printer's measure of width

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters are put in a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A juror is enlisted to judge the merits of prison reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penal reform' reads as a real policy phrase, and 'measure' as a verb; both are wordplay, with measure a printer's unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To empanel someone is to enrol them on the list of jurors chosen to hear a trial.

clue.text: Send out again for the old copy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to publish or distribute a second time, a verb
second meaning: a new edition of an earlier work, a noun

explanation.surface: An editor ordering an old text to be put out once more.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means publish anew; as a noun it is a fresh printing of an old book or record.
